summary: Hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + reranking for search relevance. Customer currently uses ElasticSearch with Pinecone for vectors; pain points: inconsistent relevance, high cost at scale, and latency spikes. We walked through Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints, console demo for monitoring token costs and per-route latency, and Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization). Customer requested security docs and a short pilot to run benchmarks against their 1K queries.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-10-02
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Redwood CSM), Ethan Moore (AuroraSearch Head of Search), Priya Singh (AuroraSearch Platform Eng), Carlos Rivera (AuroraSearch Product)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, i'll hand off to ravi to do the demo but quick round robin intros please
[00:12] Ethan: hey ethan moore, head of search at aurorasearch, we run a mix of elasticsearch and pinecone for vectors
[00:18] Priya: priya singh, platform engineering. i'm the infra owner, curious about vpc and perf implications
[00:25] Carlos: carlos rivera, product, i'm mostly focused on relevance improvements and business metrics
[00:31] Maya: great, ravi over to you

--- Demo / walkthrough ---
[00:35] Ravi: thanks maya. alright so quick agenda: show hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints, then console for observability, and finally optimize suggestions. i'll try a live rerank call with a handful of sample queries, disclaimer — network might have slight latency so bear with me
[01:05] Ravi: first, embeddings: POST /v1/embeddings, response is 1536-d vector in this model, we support batching, async ingest, etc. you'll see we auto-detect content type — but you can pass metadata fields.
[01:40] Ethan: quick q — do you store customer vectors if we use hosted? what's retention?
[01:47] Ravi: good question. hosted api has configurable retention and encryption at rest, by default we do ephemeral storage for embeddings unless you opt into long-term storage; for enterprise we also offer a private deployment. note: we encrypt with KMS and can use customer-managed keys on private deployments, for hosted we use provider KMS but we do offer bring-your-own-key via dedicated/private plans.
[02:20] Priya: so for hosted we'd need to confirm that keys are customer-owned? i thought only private supports that
[02:27] Ravi: yes for full BYOK HSM you'd go private, but we can enable customer-managed keys in some dedicated contracts; i'll follow up with the exact matrix in the security pack.

[03:05] Ravi: switching to reranking — endpoint is POST /v1/rerank where you pass query + candidates + embeddings optional; we have two modes: model-side rerank (model scores candidates) and hybrid where we do embedding similarity first then model rerank on top. live demo coming.
[03:40] [demo screen share noise — small pause]
[04:00] Ravi: ok i'm sending a batch of 50 candidate docs, doing embedding similarity with our default model, then a light rerank model to reorder by relevance. latency for this small batch is 220ms p95 in this region, tokens processed visible in the console.
[04:30] Carlos: 220ms p95 that seems promising — what's the cost per 1K queries roughly?
[04:38] Maya: i'll send a ballpark in the follow-up pricing doc; cost is a function of batch size, model choice, and caching. also our optimize engine will suggest batching levels to hit your SLO/cost sweet spot.

--- Product console ---
[05:10] Ravi: in the console here you can see per-route token breakdown, per-model latency, and KV cache hit rate. here's an example: this rerank route has a prefix cache which avoids recomputing embeddings for similar queries; you can set cache TTLs per-route.
[05:45] Priya: does that prefix cache handle user-specific privacy constraints? e.g., if we need per-tenant isolation
[05:52] Ravi: yes, we namespace caches per-tenant and you can disable shared caching; for hosted we offer per-customer tenancy and encryption. there's also RBAC and audit logs available.

[06:20] Ethan: our big pain is intermittent spikes in latency and scoring that yields bad results — we think pinecone + elastic combo isn't consistent. can you show how rerank improves MRR?
[06:34] Ravi: sure — small A/B example: we ran a canary on a product client and saw a 12% improvement in top-3 relevance. the workflow is: use embeddings to shortlist candidates by vector similarity, then rerank with the model to refine. this reduces token usage compared to scoring all docs with the model.
[07:05] Carlos: that 12% is great — curious about cold/startup cost when queries don't hit cache
[07:13] Ravi: cold miss is higher; that's where intelligent batching and pre-warming helps. Optimize suggests initial batching windows and prefix caching based on historical query distribution.

--- Security / Compliance ---
[07:45] Priya: enterprise questions: SOC 2 type II? data residency? SAML SSO? audit logs?
[07:52] Maya: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO in the pack; SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning supported; audit logs with retention tiers; for data residency we can pin region for hosted and private goes on-prem. i'll share the security pack.
[08:20] Priya: and VPC peering or private link options? we prefer private link to avoid public egress
[08:28] Ravi: we support VPC private link for dedicated customers, and VPC peering options for private installs. hosted public api uses TLS + mutual auth options if required for the contract.

--- Technical deep dive snippets ---
[09:00] Ravi: quick note on runtime: we do continuous batching, KV cache management, and quantization-friendly execution paths. our kernel selection picks optimized ops for the model and sequence length. in practice that means lower latencies at p95 for typical sequences.
[09:30] Ethan: are you doing any custom kernel work, or is it off-the-shelf?
[09:34] Ravi: mix of both, we have tuned kernels for attention and KV cache flow on our runtime; that's part of the dedicated performance delta.

[10:05] -- Live example: customer-provided query --
[10:10] Ethan: we brought a sample: "how to migrate data from postgres to bigtable" — when we run across our index it often returns docs about backup instead of migration steps
[10:18] Ravi: ok let's try. i'm uploading 1K sample queries now (simulated), running embedding-based shortlist with 100 candidates then rerank 
[10:55] [typing noises]
[11:10] Ravi: here's the before vs after. before (elastic + keyword boost) top result was a backup guide; after rerank, model surfaces migration plan docs at rank 1-3. you can see highlighted tokens where model considered procedural steps — the output isn't perfect but shows improvement.
[11:40] Priya: any idea why elastic gave backup docs priority? probably title token match weighting
[11:45] Ravi: yes, exact match weight without semantic signal. embeddings + rerank helps when semantics matter.

--- Objections and tradeoffs ---
[12:05] Carlos: ok tradeoffs — hosted vs dedicated for us? we have compliance needs but also want fast time-to-value
[12:15] Maya: typical guidance: hosted is fastest and cheap to pilot; dedicated gives predictable throughput, VPC peering, and stronger BYOK options. private for regulated, on-prem requirements. you can start hosted pilot then lift to dedicated if you need.
[12:39] Priya: performance — if we lock in p95 250ms SLO, will hosted handle bursts?
[12:46] Ravi: hosted has regional autoscaling and routing policies, but for strict SLOs dedicated/reserved pools are recommended. we can set up canary routing and fallback models to degrade gracefully.

--- Monitoring & Quality ---
[13:15] Ravi: console also ties regressions to eval prompts — you can pin a prompt set and get alerts for quality drops. that would be important for your MRR metrics.
[13:35] Ethan: do you do label-based retraining? we have click signals
[13:40] Ravi: we integrate with customer feedback loops; Optimize will surface prompt sets where quality dropped and suggest model variants or quantization changes. retraining pipeline is something customers plug into separately.

--- Pricing & Pilot ---
[14:10] Maya: for pricing we'll draft a 3-tier pilot: small (50K calls/mo), medium (500K), and pilot run for 2 weeks with a usage cap. pilot includes support from an SE to run benchmarks. i'll include sample cost numbers and a recommended model set.
[14:35] Ethan: for pilot we need a clear success criteria: 10% lift in top-3 relevance or 20% latency reduction at p95.
[14:45] Carlos: also want a cost-per-query estimate compared to our current spend

--- Logistics / timeline ---
[15:00] Maya: sounds good. next steps: we'll send pricing and security docs; ravi will share runbook; priya will provide sample queries and infra contact; target pilot week is 2028-10-16.
[15:18] Priya: can you also include a minimal infra checklist? IP allowlist, certs, endpoints etc?
[15:23] Ravi: yes — i'll attach a one-page infra checklist in the runbook.

--- Closing recap ---
[15:40] Maya: recap: demo of embeddings + rerank, console shows per-route latency and cost, optimize suggestions for batching and quantization, security pack and pilot runbook to follow. action items noted. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[15:55] Ethan: thanks all, excited to try the pilot
[15:58] Carlos: thanks
[16:00] [call ended]
